abstract: Higher-order topological states are studied in a woodpile photonic crystal (PhC) having a large complete photonic bandgap. According to theoretical predictions, we fabricate a three-dimensional all-dielectric PhC with a millimeter-scale lattice period. The structure consists of two distinct lattice types that coincide through a structural displacement, where their interface intersection gives rise to hinge states. Microwave transmission measurements reveal transmission peaks and spatial localization at the intersection, demonstrating the hinge states. Furthermore, we confirm the absence of hinge states at a specific intersection. As theoretically predicted, hinge states emerge at intersections where the localized boundary polarizations are topologically different, whereas they are absent at intersections where the boundary polarizations are equivalent.
